newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan issues 1997 term naphtha buying tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan issues 1997 term naphtha buying tender.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a term tender to buy naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) naphtha for 1997, an official said on Friday.
The official said CPC was seeking one 25,000-30,000 tonnes of N+A naphtha a month but was "quite flexible."
"If the seller can only supply one cargo quarterly or bi-monthly, we will consider it," the official said. "It depends on the price."
"But the seller needs to let us know the quantity it can supply when considering the premium," the official said.
CPC is seeking offers on a cost-and-freight basis to Kaohsiung at a premium in U.S. dollars per barrel over Singapore spot naphtha quotes.
The tender closes on November 18 and offers should be valid for two days, although the conclusion may be delayed as term deals are open to negotiation, the official said.
CPC has sought the N+A naphtha on term for several years and has been buying up to cargoes a month in 1996.
